mathematical_justification.clause: Nonzero signs and every legal Theta call
mathematical_justification.assessment: Composition strictness and boundaryIndex_injective make all three actual occurrence labels in each near/far triple distinct. For near signs these are the consecutive cut-list positions k,k+1,k+2; for far signs the middle position is strictly between0 ands. G1 therefore gives both signs nonzero without using G2. SignType has values-1,0,1, so nonzero_sign_cases yields exactly the two source signs. sign_product_nonzero derives both h*d and -h*d nonzero, and gates_nonzero explicitly records both as+1 or-1 at every actual cut. signTheta requires a proof that its SignType argument is nonzero, so no call at zero is possible on this interface. Its integer value is1 on+1 and0 on-1. The independently checked real_step_interpretation identifies its real coercion with the source positive-real step on every actual nonzero sign argument. This develops the restriction used by the gates, not an unrelated totalized value at zero or a claim to formalize a standalone step function on arbitrary nonzero reals.

ordinaryGate is the actual integer-coerced near sign d times signTheta(-h*d); rootGate uses signTheta(h*d). ordinaryWeight and rootWeight are the products of those exact factors over every interior cut. The scalar lemma checks all four allowed nonzero sign pairs and proves the two integer half formulas. Since the source fractions are ordinary exact halves, the independent real_gate_identities additionally proves both corresponding real-field equations on all four pairs. real_weight_identities transports the actual integer finite products into products of these real halves. Thus integer division introduces no rounding discrepancy: on this domain the numerators are-2,0,2 and the checked real equations hold exactly.
